intro: You've searched for the best IR35 consultant near you, which usually means you're facing a contract or working arrangement where IR35 status matters and you want expert help. Perhaps you're a contractor unsure if your limited company is caught, or a business engaging freelancers and worried about compliance. Finding a good consultant is about checking their qualifications and approach, not just a ranking.
need_heading: What people searching for an IR35 consultant usually need
need_lead: Most people want clarity on their IR35 position and confidence that they're dealing with someone competent.
needs: You're a contractor who has been offered a new contract and need to know whether it falls inside or outside IR35 before you sign.
You're a hiring business engaging a freelancer through their limited company and want to avoid being caught by off-payroll working rules.
You've received a letter from HMRC querying your IR35 status and need support during an enquiry.
Your working practices have changed and you're unsure if your original IR35 assessment still holds.
You want a written assessment you can rely on and keep for your records.
context_heading: What 'best' means when choosing an IR35 consultant
context: There is no official ranking of IR35 consultants, so 'best' is a matter of judging qualifications and experience for yourself. 'Tax adviser' is not a protected title, but you can look for membership of specialist bodies such as the Chartered Institute of Taxation or the Association of Taxation Technicians, whose members follow a shared code of professional conduct.

It's also reasonable to ask whether the consultant is supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes, as paid tax advisers must be, and whether they hold professional indemnity insurance. A good consultant will explain their reasoning clearly and put their advice in writing.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Describe your situation: whether you're a contractor or a hiring business, and what type of work is involved.
Mention the specific contract or working arrangement that's worrying you, including any key terms like substitution or control.
Say whether you've already had an IR35 assessment or received any correspondence from HMRC.
Explain what you're hoping to achieve, such as a written opinion, help with a contract assessment, or support during an enquiry.
Indicate any deadlines you're working towards, such as a contract start date or a response deadline from HMRC.
Let us know if you have a preference for a consultant near you or are happy to work remotely.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the IR35 consultant
questions: What qualifications and specialist body memberships do you hold?
Will you provide a written assessment of my IR35 status?
How do you keep your knowledge up to date with changes to IR35 rules?
What is your experience of supporting clients during HMRC enquiries?
Do you hold professional indemnity insurance?
How do you charge for your work, and what will I receive for the fee?

faqs.q: How do I judge who is the best IR35 consultant for me?
faqs.a: There is no official ranking, so look at qualifications, membership of a specialist body, experience with situations like yours, and whether they'll give you clear written advice. Ask about supervision and insurance, and trust your judgment about how well they explain things.

faqs.q: What does an IR35 consultant actually do?
faqs.a: They assess contracts and working practices to determine whether IR35 applies, provide written status assessments, and can support you during an HMRC enquiry. They help both contractors and the businesses that engage them.

No, 'tax adviser' is not a protected title in the UK. However, members of bodies like the Chartered Institute of Taxation or the Association of Taxation Technicians follow a shared code of professional conduct, and paid tax advisers must be supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes.
